steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Problem questions present a factual scenario and ask you to advise on the legal position — they test your ability to apply law to facts, not just recall legal rules

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The ILAC method provides a clear structure: Issue (identify the legal question), Law (state the relevant legal rules), Application (apply the law to the facts), Conclusion (state the likely outcome)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Identify all the legal issues in the scenario — there are usually multiple issues, such as actus reus, mens rea and any defences in a criminal problem

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: State the law accurately — name the relevant statute or case, define the legal principle precisely and set out the elements that must be proved

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the ILAC method and why is it useful? | Q: How should you approach a criminal law problem question? | Q: Why is it important to use the specific facts from the scenario?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the scenario at least twice — once to get the overall picture and once to identify each legal issue and relevant fact Use the ILAC structure for each issue in the scenario — do not mix issues together Always apply the law to the facts — this is where most marks are gained; stating the law alone is not enough Acknowledge both sides where the outcome is uncertain — show the examiner you can argue from both the prosecution and defence perspectives Underline key facts in the scenario as you read — these are the triggers for specific legal points
